items.output: {"root_cause": "rating-api v4.31.0 added a per-request audit write to Postgres, which roughly doubled connection hold time per request. The service's connection pool (DB_POOL_SIZE=20) saturated, requests queued waiting for a connection and then timed out after 5s. Postgres itself is healthy -- 97 of 400 connections in use, CPU at 33%.", "category": "resource-exhaustion", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "harbor-api v10.2.0 introduced an in-process feature-vector cache keyed by user_id with no size bound or eviction. It grew monotonically with unique users until the JVM heap hit its 1856m ceiling inside a 2Gi container limit, producing long GC pauses and then OOMKills, which is what put the pods into a crash loop. The drop in tracking-store calls from 680/s to 88/s confirms the cache is the new code path.", "category": "resource-exhaustion", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "tariff-dispatcher v8.8.0 creates a new HTTP client session per outbound request for TLS pinning and never closes it, leaking one socket per delivery. File descriptors climbed steadily from 410 to the 65536 limit over roughly a day, after which no new connection could be opened and deliveries began failing. Memory, CPU and restart count are all normal, so this is descriptor exhaustion specifically rather than general resource pressure.", "category": "resource-exhaustion", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "insight-sink v4.1.0 began writing full request bodies to a local log on ip-10-17-15-223 at roughly 44 MiB/s and shipped without a logrotate config, so /var/log/audit/requests.log grew to 197GB and filled the node's 200GB disk. Kubelet then evicted pods by priority, which took out three tariff-api pods. tariff-api is the victim; insight-sink is the cause.", "category": "resource-exhaustion", "action_id": "clear_disk_space"}

{"root_cause": "consent-gateway v12.1.0 added a per-request geoip lookup using a synchronous client library, called directly from the async request handler. Each ~390ms lookup blocks the event loop, so event loop lag went from 4ms to 970ms and throughput collapsed from 4200 to 620 req/s while CPU fell from 48% to 14%. atlas-service itself is healthy and responding at its normal latency.", "category": "resource-exhaustion", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "A config-only push 22 minutes before the alert set SMTP_HOST to smtp-relay.staging.internal. The staging relay rejects the production sender domain with SMTP 550, so email delivery collapsed while push, which does not use SMTP, stayed healthy. The production relay is fine -- its accepted message rate fell simply because nothing is being sent to it any more.", "category": "config-error", "action_id": "revert_config_change"}

{"root_cause": "The orders_enrich_line_items flag, rolled from 5% to 100% over the hour before the alert, issues one query per line item instead of a single batched fetch. Queries per request climbed from 3 to 470 and Postgres query volume from 2600/s to 408000/s while mean query duration stayed flat at 4ms, so this is query volume rather than slow queries. Latency scales with account size because larger orders have more line items.", "category": "bad-release", "action_id": "disable_feature_flag"}

{"root_cause": "The Helm chart 3.0.0 upgrade restructured values.yaml and dropped the REGION value, so SESSION_STORE_HOST fell back to the compiled-in default rewards-store.us-east-1.internal. fleet-service now crosses from ap-southeast-2 to us-east-1 on every request, adding about 200ms of network round trip. rewards-store itself answers in 3-4ms in both regions.", "category": "config-error", "action_id": "revert_config_change"}

{"root_cause": "The TLS certificate for dispatch-service.prod.internal had not_after 2026-09-16T00:00:00Z and auto_renew disabled, so it expired exactly at midnight. signup-service now rejects the handshake with an x509 expiry error and every call fails. Both services are otherwise healthy -- their CPU fell because they are doing no work, and an expiry warning fired seven days earlier and was not actioned.", "category": "dependency-failure", "action_id": "rotate_certificate"}

{"root_cause": "review-api v6.0.0 renamed stock_count to available_units and changed quantity to a string, a breaking response-schema change. storefront validates the old schema and rejects every v3 response, which is why its error rate tracked the rollout from 22% to 61% as v3 went from 35% to 100% of pods. review-api is serving healthy 200s at 13ms -- correct by its own contract, incompatible with its consumer's.", "category": "dependency-failure", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "Traffic rose roughly 6x from 2100 to 12400 req/s. The HPA scaled voucher-api to its maxReplicas of 12 and then emitted FailedRescale because it wanted 24. With scaling capped, per-pod CPU pinned at 94%, the containers began hitting CPU throttling at 3.1 s/s, and latency degraded. Nothing is broken -- the service is simply capped below the capacity the load requires, and invoice-store is healthy at 26ms.", "category": "capacity", "action_id": "adjust_hpa"}

{"root_cause": "transcoder is memory-bound -- each job needs about 3.2GiB against a 4Gi limit -- so memory utilisation sits at 98% and jobs are deferred for lack of memory, dropping concurrency from 12 to 3 and throughput from 88 to 21 jobs/min against a steady 95/min arrival rate. The HPA is configured on CPU only, and CPU never leaves 38%, so it holds at 6 replicas and never scales despite having headroom to 40.", "category": "capacity", "action_id": "adjust_hpa"}

{"root_cause": "The audit_events table grew from 4.1M to 78M rows over two weeks. The tenant-scoped search query filters on tenant_id and created_at with no supporting index, so Postgres falls back to a sequential scan -- confirmed by the logged plan and by seq scans rising from 0.3/s to 14/s. The buffer cache hit ratio fell from 99.4% to 71.2% because each scan evicts the working set. Request rate is flat, so this is data volume, not load.", "category": "data-layer", "action_id": "add_database_index"}

{"root_cause": "The insight-migrator backfill job started an ALTER TABLE accounts ADD COLUMN with a NOT NULL DEFAULT, which rewrites the table and holds an AccessExclusiveLock on accounts for the whole rewrite -- now 840 seconds and counting on backend pid 39001. Every write queues behind that lock and hits the statement timeout, while reads served from before the lock stay fast at 6ms. Connections climbed to 398 of 400 because blocked writers hold theirs.", "category": "data-layer", "action_id": "kill_long_running_query"}

{"root_cause": "The prod-default-deny NetworkPolicy was rebuilt from service annotations and went from 19 allow rules to 12, dropping the identity-auth to promo-scorer rule. Packets are now silently discarded, so identity-auth sees connect timeouts while promo-scorer sits ready with exactly zero inbound requests and 2% CPU. Neither service deployed; the change was a network policy revision.", "category": "network", "action_id": "update_network_policy"}

{"root_cause": "The CoreDNS Corefile update lowered ndots from 5 to 1 and dropped the cluster.local search domains. Callers that use short names like \"storage-service\" no longer have those names completed and get NXDOMAIN, while the same code paths using fully-qualified names still resolve -- which is why failures look intermittent and spread across unrelated upstreams. Every upstream service is healthy; their request volume fell only because callers cannot resolve them.", "category": "network", "action_id": "revert_config_change"}

{"root_cause": "A 3-minute Elasticsearch GC pause around 27 minutes before the alert caused a brief batch of search timeouts. rewards-bff, which since yesterday retries 5 times with no backoff, amplified that into roughly 6x offered load: its user request rate stayed flat at about 2100/s while its outbound search rate went from 2100/s to 12300/s and its retry rate from 5/s to 10200/s. listing-service saturated and now rejects requests, which generates more retries. Elastic- search recovered within three minutes and is healthy at 84ms; the incident is sustained entirely by the retry loop.", "category": "cascading-failure", "action_id": "reduce_retry_aggressiveness"}

{"root_cause": "atlas-service v10.6.0 warms the entire price cache on boot and writes every key with the same fixed 3600s TTL and zero jitter. All keys therefore expire simultaneously one hour after boot and each hour after that: about 41000 keys expire at once, cache hit ratio drops from 99% to 2%, and every concurrent request falls through to signup-db, which jumps from 180 to 24000 queries/s and 97% CPU for about 90 seconds until the cache refills. Request volume is flat throughout, so this is expiry synchronisation, not load.", "category": "cascading-failure", "action_id": "rollback_deploy"}

{"root_cause": "The spring campaign launched by harbor-blast 75 minutes ago sends 1.4M promotional messages at concurrency 400 with no sender-side rate limiting, taking cedar-gateway from 124 to 3100 sends/s and consuming 100% of the provider's 180000/hour quota. The provider now returns 429 for everything on the shared path, so OTP traffic -- flat at about 98 sends/s throughout -- fails alongside the campaign. cedar-gateway has no priority queueing, so bulk and critical traffic compete equally for the same quota.", "category": "dependency-failure", "action_id": "shed_load"}

{"root_cause": "Node ip-10-24-7-217 lost NTP sync about four hours ago and its clock has drifted 7.4 seconds behind. The two dispatch-service pods on that node see freshly issued tokens as not yet valid because the nbf claim is in their past-shifted future, so they reject them. That node hosts 2 of 16 pods, which matches the steady 12% rejection rate, and retries succeed because they land on a correctly-synced pod. voucher-issuer is healthy and the tokens are valid.", "category": "misleading-signal", "action_id": "drain_node"}

{"root_cause": "The Prometheus relabel change renamed the job label from 'service' to 'k8s_service', but the promo-service alert rule still selects on service='promo-service' and now matches nothing, so its series report zero. promo-service is serving normally -- ledger-gateway measures 870 req/s to it at 17ms with a 0.04% error rate, its own logs show continuing 200s, and nimbus-store sees unchanged downstream traffic. Every metric that went to zero comes from the affected scrape config; every independent signal is normal. This is a monitoring artefact, not an incident.", "category": "false-alarm", "action_id": "fix_monitoring_config"}
